entities.note: No credentials observed in any source. scope.json does not set authentication_required, so authentication is out of scope, not a vulnerability. Each source is treated as an independent demo session against the shared order fixture.

visible_constraints: You may qualify for a $30.00 adjustment.
observed_changes: Price protection status changed from Eligible to Adjustment issued
Order summary Price adjustment changed from $0.00 to $30.00
Total returned appeared with status message Price adjustment issued.

visible_constraints: Cancel dialog states: 'A $100.00 reimbursement will be sent to the original payment method.'
observed_changes: status 'Order canceled and reimbursement issued.' appeared
Order actions collapsed to 'This order has no actions requiring your attention.'

visible_constraints: Refund request creates a $100.00 refund request for review
observed_changes: Shipment changed from Delivered to Refund pending

visible_constraints: Your refund request is ready to be processed
The $100.00 refund will be sent to the original payment method
observed_changes: Order actions changed to no actions requiring your attention

inferred_relationships.description: After a price adjustment is issued, the Cancel order affordance is removed from the order page. This is a UI-observed lock; whether the server enforces it server-side is unverified.
Price protection is a one-time eligibility: once an adjustment is issued, the Request price adjustment affordance disappears.
After the order is canceled, all customer order actions are removed and the UI shows 'This order has no actions requiring your attention.'
The cancel action offers a single, fixed $100.00 reimbursement to the original payment method.
Price protection is not available while another order request is active; the price-adjustment action is removed after cancellation.
Refund completion is gated behind a prior refund request in the UI; the Complete refund button appears only after a refund request exists.

Agent inference (unverified): the sum of cancellation reimbursement, price adjustment, and completed refund must not exceed originalAmount ($100). Each single action in isolation reaches at most totalReturned=100, so the single-source recordings do not violate the cap; only cross-source composed sequences are capable of violating it.

contradictions.description: The cancel-flow state map marks /api/order/refund/request and /api/order/refund/complete as inferred (not exercised in the cancel recording) and lists them as conflicting actions co-visible at UI step 1. The refund-flow state map exercises both refund actions on the same order ID and treats the complete action as observed. The cross-flow analysis treats refund/request and refund/complete as observed (per refund run), not inferred.
contradictions.resolution: Treat the refund endpoints as observed via the refund source run; the cancel-run's 'inferred' labels only reflect what that single run captured, not global availability.

contradictions.description: In the price source, after a price adjustment, availableActions.requestRefund remains true, but availableActions.cancelOrder and availableActions.requestPriceAdjustment are set to false. In the cancel source, after cancellation, availableActions.requestRefund is false. The UI affordance state is not a simple 'any action locks all others' — only some pairwise locks are observed.
contradictions.resolution: Record the observed pairwise locks as they appear; do not assume a global 'all actions locked' invariant. The cross-flow tests will determine whether the server enforces each pairwise lock.

contradictions.description: All three recordings operate on order id=1042 with the same initial fixture. The recordings were not made in a single continuous session — they were independent resets of the same fixture. No single HAR contains both a cancel and a price adjustment, or a cancel and a refund, in one session.
contradictions.resolution: The cross-flow analysis composes these independent observations into hypothetical composed sequences. The backend fixture (POST /api/demo/reset) is assumed to restore the same initial state; each mutation script establishes its own fresh state via that reset before composing its sequence.

setup_note: POST /api/demo/reset is the documented setup path for restoring the demo order fixture. It is never an attack target and may only be invoked to establish a clean precondition for each scenario.

critical_endpoints.why: Observed payout action (price source): issues a $30 adjustment that raises totalReturned from 0 to 30 and locks price adjustment + cancellation. Agent inference (unverified): composed with cancel or refund completion, the $30 may stack past originalAmount=100.

Observed payout action (cancel source): issues a $100 reimbursement that sets totalReturned to 100 and locks all customer actions. Agent inference (unverified): composed with price adjustment or refund completion, a second payout may raise totalReturned past 100.

Observed payout-initiation action (refund source): creates a $100 refund request (requestedAmount=100, status=pending) and enables completeRefund. Agent inference (unverified): composed with a prior price adjustment, the pending $100 refund plus the already-paid $30 adjustment may exceed originalAmount=100 once complete is called.

Observed payout-completion action (refund source): completes a pending $100 refund, raising totalReturned from 0 to 100. Highest financial impact per action. Agent inference (unverified): composed with a prior price adjustment or a prior cancellation, the $100 refund completion may push totalReturned past originalAmount=100.
